Subject: Post-demo handoff: model runway & context sizing for Finovatics

Hi Rachel / Samir —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday; really appreciated the product tour and the clarity on your key read/write patterns. As promised, I’m opening the handoff thread between CS/Onboarding and our implementation team. Goal: agree the initial model shortlist, expected context runway (95th/99th pctiles), and a 3‑month token runway so we can size Dedicated vs Hosted for your initial launch.

Quick asks to unblock sizing: please confirm the following if you can — ideally by EOD today or tomorrow morning:
- Average user prompt length (tokens) and sample prompt examples (we’ll use to estimate prefix vs completion split)
- 95th / 99th percentile context window (do you expect long histories or mostly single-turn?)
- Current monthly API calls and a realistic peak p95 qps for live traffic (or expected transactions per minute)
- Any compliance constraints that would force a Private deployment (e.g., on-prem, VPC, KMS)

I’ve attached a short onboarding questionnaire to capture the above. Internal folks I’ve looped: Monica (CS lead) who’ll own the mutual action plan, and the implementation lead will be in follow-ups.

Next steps from our side: Monica and I will draft a lightweight model shortlist + estimated token volumes based on your answers; we’ll include cost delta between hosted vs reserved Dedicated for peak-hour scenarios.

Thanks —
David

Hi David —

Thanks — attaching the items you asked for. TL;DR answers inline:
- Average prompt length: ~120 tokens (most users send short queries). Attached: sample_prompt_examples.json.
- 95th percentile context need: ~2,500 tokens; 99th ~6,400 tokens (we have a small set of long multi-turn sessions).
- Current monthly API calls (production): ~1.2M calls/month. Peak observed p95: ~45 QPS; planned launch spike could briefly hit ~120 QPS for 10–15 minutes when a new campaign goes live. Attached: monthly_volume_report.csv.
- Compliance: standard SOC2 + customer data is pseudonymized; no on‑prem requirement today — VPC preferred later but not required for MVP.

Samir, forwarding to Procurement for any contractual items. Let us know if you need more telemetry (e.g., request size distribution).

Best,
Rachel

David / Grace —

Thanks for the inputs from Finovatics. I ran a quick sizing pass based on Rachel’s numbers and the sample prompts. High-level recommendation for the initial 12‑week runway:

Model shortlist (reasoning):
- redwood-chat-13b-q4 (primary): strong quality/latency balance for short prompts; quantized to q4 to reduce GPU memory footprint. Good for 80–90% of requests.
- redwood-base-7b-8k (economy): for cost-sensitive batch completions and heavier caching; fits a 8k context window for the 95th use cases.
- llama2-70b-8bit (fallback for long context): nominate as a regional fallback for the 99th cases that need 6k+ context — use sparingly due to cost.

Sizing and token forecast (conservative):
- Per-request token mix (estimate from samples): prompt 120 tokens, response 160 tokens average -> ~280 tokens per call.
- Baseline monthly tokens = 1.2M calls * 280 = ~336M tokens/month.
- Plan for growth + spikes: provision runway for 2x baseline = ~672M tokens/month to cover campaigns and growth for first quarter.
- Peak concurrency: use 120 QPS burst for 15m -> provision routing/fallback rules and warm-up windows; suggest 8–12 Dedicated GPUs if we want <150ms p95 for redwood-chat-13b-q4 under burst, otherwise host and autoscale with throttling.

Operational notes:
- KV/prefix caching: many requests are short and highly repetitive — we should enable prefix caching and a short-term hot-cache to reduce token compute on the primary model.
- Context window strategy: keep short-turn history in request for accuracy; offload long historical context to retrieval + condensed summary to stay within 8k where possible.

Ask to you both:
- David, can you surface any customer SLAs that would mandate dedicated reserved capacity? If not, we’ll propose a hybrid hosted-first with a reserved Dedicated buffer during campaigns.
- Grace, can you prepare a quick cost delta (hosted vs 3-month reserved) and a suggested canary rollout cadence?

I’ll draft the mutual action plan once Grace confirms the cost figures; we should aim to lock the shortlist and MA P by Fri.

—Monica
Monica Patel

Rachel / Samir —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and helpful artifacts. Monica and Grace have proposed the shortlist below and we’re ready to move to a formal kickoff. Attach: mutual_action_plan_v1.docx and the model cost workbook.

Short summary of agreed plan:
- Shortlist: redwood-chat-13b-q4 (primary), redwood-base-7b-8k (economy), llama2-70b-8bit (fallback).
- Runway: provision for ~700M tokens/month for Q1 of launch; revisit after 30 days of production telemetry.
- Burst handling: reserve a small Dedicated buffer for campaign spikes (we’ll propose numbers in the MAP) and use smart routing to fall back to economy models when needed.
- Next steps: 1) schedule 60-minute onboarding kickoff (implementation, infra, security) — propose Mon 20 Sep 10:00 PT or Tue 21 Sep 11:00 PT; 2) Finovatics to confirm sample dataset access and any IP redaction rules; 3) Procurement to review MAP and cost workbook.

Rachel — can you confirm Tues/Wed availability for the kickoff and whether Procurement needs any additional paperwork before the meeting?

Thanks —
David
